context:
Goal: a test's verdict never depends on how fast the machine is.
Problem (rule): decision test-practices P5 bans every wall-clock wait in a test. PR #1177 rewrites P5 to allow a "hang guard": a wait limit that only stops a test that hangs. It cites only a plan line, not your ruling. A reviewer showed that a speed limit can pass as a hang guard just by its label.
Based on (read): docs/decisions/test-practices.md P5 on main; docs/plans/time-pinned-tests.md; 252 existing wait limits in tests.
Departs from: main's P5, which bans every wall-clock wait — a and b allow a hang-guard limit; c keeps P5 and converts the 252 limits to outcome checks.
Meanwhile lane cs-revive-unfinished ships #1177's finder fix and leaves P5's text alone.

options.label: Allow hang guards as written
options.lose: A speed limit can hide as a hang guard. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.

options.gain: Real hang guards stay, and speed limits get caught: each limit must be several times the measured run, with the figure beside it, as CI job limits already require.
options.label: Allow them with a size rule
options.lose: One more rule to check. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.

options.gain: The rule stays strict, and the tests meet it: step time-pinned-tests-go converts each of the 252 wait limits to a check on the outcome, over time.
options.label: Keep P5 and change the tests (recommended)
options.lose: More test rewrites, and the limits break P5's text until they are converted.

reply: Answered in chat at 13:00 CST, with none of the options: P5 never meant to ban timed waits. A timed test is allowed, and catching a hung test is a good reason for one. A test whose verdict depends on speed uses a synthetic clock, so machine load cannot change it. Lane cs-revive-unfinished rewrites decision test-practices P5 in #1177. Step time-pinned-tests-go now converts speed-dependent waits to a synthetic clock and keeps hang guards.
short: Test hang guards: keep the ban and convert the 252 limits?
title: May a test keep a wait limit that only stops a hung test (a hang guard)?
why: PR #1177 changes your test rule without your ruling, so only you can say yes or no.
